summary.one_liner: WebVM is a Linux virtual machine that runs entirely in the browser via WebAssembly, booting an unmodified Debian image using the CheerpX x86-to-WebAssembly engine.
summary.what_it_does: The repository hosts the source for WebVM, a serverless x86 Linux environment running client-side in HTML5/WebAssembly. It is powered by CheerpX, which provides an x86-to-WebAssembly JIT compiler, a virtual block-based file system, a Linux syscall emulator, and sandboxed execution. Users have root by default, and the README describes Debian images with native development toolchains, plus an Alpine/Xorg/i3 graphical environment. Networking is built on Tailscale, with optional use of an exit node for internet access and support for self-hosted Headscale control servers. The README also covers deploying a fork to GitHub Pages, building custom .ext2 disk images from a Dockerfile, serving locally with nginx, and an optional Claude AI integration in the UI that requires a user-supplied API key.
use_cases: Run a Linux shell or dev toolchain in a browser tab
Host a custom Linux environment on GitHub Pages
Build a browser-based Python REPL from a Dockerfile
Access a private Tailscale network from a web VM
Experiment with x86 binaries and CTF challenges in the browser
Demo or teach Linux without server-side infrastructure
how_to_run: Download the debian_mini .ext2 image from Releases into custom-disk-images/
Edit config_public_terminal.js to set diskImageUrl and diskImageType = "bytes"
nginx -p . -c nginx.conf, then open the local URL in a browser
notable: Runs an unmodified Debian distribution in the browser with no server-side compute
Tailscale integration lets the browser VM reach a private network and, with an exit node, the internet
A GitHub Actions Deploy workflow builds custom .ext2 images from any Dockerfile and publishes to Pages or Releases
Setting CMD in the Dockerfile to /usr/bin/python3 yields a Python REPL deployment
Immutable builds: versions tied to the CheerpX npm package stay working
caveats: Some low-level networking such as ICMP ping is not available; use curl or wget instead
dockerfiles/debian_large is too large for GitHub Pages
CheerpX public deployment is free only for individual exploration; organizations, including non-profits and academia, need a license, and hosting a CheerpX build elsewhere needs a commercial license
